subject: Biology
question_summary: Direct question testing which inhibitor increases Km without changing Vmax and competes with substrate.
source_excerpt: MDCAT 2021 Paper Code A, Question 42: Competitive inhibitors have structural resemblance with substrate, increasing apparent Km while Vmax remains unchanged.

subject: Biology
concept: Overcoming Competitive Inhibition with Excess Substrate
question_summary: Application scenario: An enzymatic reaction is inhibited; adding high substrate restores original reaction velocity.
source_excerpt: MDCAT 2023 Paper Code C, Question 19: The effect of competitive inhibitors can be reversed by increasing substrate concentration.

subject: Biology
question_summary: Testing difference between active site competition and allosteric site binding regarding Vmax reduction.
source_excerpt: NUMS 2024 Paper Code B, Question 31: Non-competitive inhibitors bind to allosteric sites, decreasing Vmax without altering Km.

subject: Biology
concept: Mitochondrial Structure - Krebs Cycle Site and ATP Synthase Cristae
question_summary: Direct question testing compartmentalization: where Krebs cycle reactions and ATP synthase complexes reside in mitochondria.
source_excerpt: MDCAT 2022 Paper Code B, Question 18: In eukaryotic mitochondria, the enzymes of the Krebs cycle are located in the soluble matrix, while ATP synthase (F0-F1 particles) and electron transport chain components are embedded in the inner mitochondrial membrane cristae.

subject: Biology
concept: Endosymbiotic Evidence of Mitochondria (Circular mtDNA and 70S Ribosomes)
question_summary: Testing molecular characteristics that support the endosymbiotic origin of mitochondria.
source_excerpt: NUMS 2023 Paper Code A, Question 9: Mitochondria resemble prokaryotic cells because they contain circular double-stranded DNA (mtDNA), bacterial-type 70S ribosomes, and divide autonomously through binary fission.

subject: Physics
concept: Newton's Third Law - Why Action and Reaction Never Cancel
question_summary: Direct question testing why equal and opposite action-reaction forces do not cancel each other.
source_excerpt: MDCAT 2022 Paper Code A, Question 14: Action and reaction forces never cancel or balance each other because they always act on two different interacting bodies simultaneously.

subject: Physics
concept: Rocket Propulsion and Momentum Conservation via Newton's Third Law
question_summary: Application scenario evaluating rocket thrust in vacuum space as action-reaction pair.
source_excerpt: NUMS 2023 Paper Code C, Question 28: A rocket accelerates forward in vacuum because the backward force of escaping exhaust gases exerts an equal and opposite forward reaction thrust force on the rocket.

subject: Chemistry
concept: Ionization Energy Anomaly - Nitrogen vs Oxygen (Half-filled Subshell)
question_summary: Conceptual question testing the electronic configuration reason for higher first ionization energy in Nitrogen than Oxygen.
source_excerpt: MDCAT 2023 Paper Code A, Question 8: Nitrogen has a higher first ionization energy than oxygen because of the extra thermodynamic stability associated with its half-filled 2p3 orbital subshell.
